newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Elf sees strong flow from new Angola well.
newsitem.headline: Elf sees strong flow from new Angola well.

text.p: French oil company Elf Aquitaine's appraisal well off the Angola coast is capable of becoming the country's most productive single deep-water well, a senior Elf official said on Tuesday.
"This find is very, very good," Jean-Jacques Biteau, Elf's Explorations Director in Angola told Reuters.
"At the present flow rate of 18,000 barrels per day the new well is producing more than any deep well in the country," he said.

Elf announced last Tuesday it had struck oil at a second tier in the Girassol field on Block 17 in 1,300 metres (4,265 feet) of water northwest of Luanda. Tests confirmed the existence of a reservoir discovered in April 1996.
Production tests showed a cumulative daily flow rate of 18,000 barrels of oil per day on two reservoirs of good quality.
Most offshore wells in Angola have so far been drilled in shallow waters, Biteau said.
British Petroleum Director General in Angola, Richard Field, said the find showed the potential of Angola's deep water blocks.
BP Exploration Angola holds a 16.67 percent stake in Block 17 which also has five other oil prospectors currently involved under Elf Exploration Angola -- a subsidiary of Elf Aquitaine.
Elf is operator of Block 17 in which it has a 35 percent stake.
"If this flow rate keeps up then this is a sign of what the deep water might hold," Field said.
Elf is also drilling a deviated well at the same site to further define the size of the oil structure. Test results should be known within three weeks.
The deep water of Girassol requires an output of at least 10,000 barrels per day (bpd) per well to ensure a return on investments, Elf geologist Pierre Zarolinska said.

"If we can keep up this 18,000 barrels it will be excellent and gives us every reason to go forward with widening our exploration of the field," Zarolinska said, adding that production on Block 17 was likely to start around the year 2000.
Elf officials refused to comment on the estimated size of the field, saying they only had data showing the size of the structure and could not release that data.
Editor of Angola's Energy review magazine and a close watcher of the industry, Jose de Oliveira, put the field's reserves at a billion barrels.
"The second appraisal well indicated that there is around one billion barrels in reserve," de Oliveira said.
Other partners in the Girassol exploration include the Esso unit of U.S.-based Exxon, Den Norske Stats Oljeselskap ASA (Statoil), Norsk Hydro ASA and Belgium's Fina Inc.
